entries.text: The lantern gutters. Vaelmoor keeps what you found.
The water closes over your light without a sound.
You were the fourth Keeper this season. The others are still down here.
Somewhere far above, a bell rings once for you.
The catacombs rearrange themselves around your body, politely.
Your gear is already being catalogued by something with too many hands.
Essence leaks out of you and into the stone. It will be spent well.
The dark does not gloat. It simply resumes.
You died the way you lived: slightly too deep, slightly too late.
The lantern was the last thing to go. It always is.
A warden pokes you once with a spear, to be sure.
The floor's guardian returns to its post. The post is you, now.
Depth 4 of 5. So close that the failure will echo for a while.
Something down here has been waiting a very long time for a Keeper to fall.
The lantern burns brighter, and so do you.
Essence knits into muscle and nerve.
You understand the descent a little better than the descent understands you.
The Keeper's training returns to your hands, unbidden.
You feel, for one breath, like the sort of person who survives this.
Something old nods approvingly and says nothing.
Your wounds close. The lesson does not.
Vaelmoor feeds you just enough to keep the game interesting.
You pick up the rhythm of the place. It is a marching rhythm.
Power arrives quietly, like a tide under a door.
Another notch on a belt nobody will ever count.
The dungeon measures you again, and adjusts its bet.
The blade is pitted, but it wants to be used.
This belonged to someone who stopped needing it.
Gold still warm from a pocket that is not here.
It fits your hand as though it were made twice.
The Warrens do not give gifts. They give delays.
A Keeper's mark, stamped small in the leather.
Whatever killed the last owner, it did not take this.
The metal hums very faintly, the way the deep water does.
Ugly. Functional. Available. Choose two.
Someone has scratched a tally on it. The tally is long.
It smells of lamp oil and old rain.
The gem is cracked, and the crack is the interesting part.
This is the sort of thing you find where nobody was buried properly.
Take it. The dark has no use for it and you do.
Heavier than it looks, and it looks heavy.
A fine thing to owe your life to, if it comes to that.
A stone face with no eyes waits patiently for your offering.
The candles have burned for a hundred years on no wax at all.
Place your hand on the idol. It is warmer than stone should be.
The prayer is written in a script that hurts to follow.
Something grants your wish and immediately takes its fee.
The shrine drinks your essence and smiles with no mouth.
A Keeper knelt here once. The groove in the floor remembers his knees.
Every offering makes the shrine a little more awake.
The god of this place is small, local, and very much at home.
You feel watched by something that has no eyes but excellent ears.
The blessing settles over you like a wet coat.
The idol turns its head a fraction. It was not facing you before.
The stairs are held, and the thing holding them has been told about you.
It was a person once. The Vaults finish what the city started.
The floor stops moving. This is never a good sign.
A guardian wakes, and the whole level feels it stand up.
Three of its ribs are doorframes from a chapel it ate.
It speaks in the voice of everyone who died on this floor.
The key hangs at its waist, and the waist is forty feet of coil.
Behind it, the staircase down. It knows exactly what that means to you.
The air goes heavy, as before a storm that never breaks.
It has guarded these stairs for longer than the city has had a name.
One of its arms ends in the last Keeper's lantern, still lit.

The kraken of the deep has claimed this tomb. Its tentacles curl through the corridors like roots through soil.
Coral grows where the leviathan rests. The thing that wears the reef is patient beyond reckoning.
It whispers of tides that have long since receded.
The bite that swallowed the city still hungers.
The ocean's sovereignty made manifest.
Concentrated fury in a glass vial.
The heart that never stopped beating.
